title: Open a robot vacuum's brush door to clean its rollers: squeeze both catch buttons in before swinging it up
instruction: The robot vacuum is upside down for brush cleaning. Open its brush door so the rollers can come out, and leave the door standing open.
context: Robot vacuums need their brush rollers cleaned of wound-in hair about once a month, and the first step is opening the brush door. iRobot's Roomba i7 owner's guide: "Pinch the brush frame release tab, lift the tab, and remove any obstructions" (clean the brushes "once a month (twice a month if you have a pet)"). The i7's brush door is a narrow arm at the rollers' end, hinged at its front end; its rear end is held by a spring catch whose two green buttons stick out of either side of it in small finger recesses. Both buttons must be held squeezed in while the door's end is lifted: pulling the end without squeezing gets nowhere (the catch hooks under the recesses' floors), squeezing one is not enough, and letting go before lifting lets it catch again. Then the door has to be turned up about its hinge, the hand turning with it, until it stands open past upright.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the bench top. An iRobot Roomba i7 robot vacuum (339 across, 3.4 kg; switched off) lies upside down on the bench, as its owner's guide shows for brush cleaning, its footprint centred at x 233, y 50, its front (caster) toward the robot; its underside, now on top, is 80 above the bench. Across its middle lies the cleaning head: two green rubber brush rollers (25 across, 184 long) side by side across the robot (along y), the front one dark green, the rear one light green, their tops 2 below the underside. At the rollers' left end lies the brush door: a black arm 16 wide (y 144 to 160), 94 long (x 197 to 291) and 14 thick, flush with the underside, hinged at its front end on a pin across it (at x 205, 7 below the underside), covering the rollers' bearing ends. Its rear end is held by the spring catch: two green buttons, 14 long and 15 tall, standing 3.5 out of either side of the door's end (x 273 to 287), sprung outward (2.0 N, 3.4 N squeezed flush), each in a finger recess 18 wide, 30 long and 16 deep beside the door's end; below each button a tongue reaches 3 under the recess's floor. With both buttons squeezed flush both tongues clear the floors and the door lifts; it turns up to 100 degrees (just past upright) and stays where it is put. Also on the underside: the two drive wheels in their wells either side of the cleaning head (72 across, 15 proud), the front caster, the side brush's hub and the bin's bottom. Every collider is listed in README.md.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run with a protractor at the door's hinge and a ruler. The door's angle is measured between the door and the vacuum's underside. 1.0 (success): the door open at least 80 degrees, both grippers at least 3 cm clear of the door and its buttons, the vacuum in place (its centre within 40 mm of its start, its underside within 10 degrees of level), and the door and the vacuum still (the door's angle within 0.5 degrees and the vacuum within 2 mm over 1 s), all held for 1 s. 0.5: the door open at least 30 degrees with the vacuum in place (including open 80 or more but still held or moving). 0.25: the door lifted at least 5 degrees (the catch released) with the vacuum in place. 0: anything else: the door shut (under 5 degrees; caught, it cannot lift more than half a degree), or the vacuum dragged more than 40 mm, tipped more than 10 degrees or knocked off the bench.
reset_notes: Swing the brush door down until both catch buttons click under the recess floors, then set the vacuum back upside down at its marked place. Nothing is consumed or fastened.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The vacuum's body (iRobot's size) is fixed where it lies: at 3.4 kg the arms' few newtons cannot shift or tip it. iRobot publishes no drawings of the door, so its size and 12 g mass, the buttons and recesses, the tongues' 3 mm hook, the springs (2.0-3.4 N), the hinge friction (0.010 N m), the 100 degree stop and the rollers' size are estimates from photos, to be measured on a real i7. The rollers are fixed parts of the body.
